---
title: "Reproducibility with restricted-access data"
date: 2026-07-01
categories: [methods, reproducibility]
---

Parts of this research use data accessed through the Centre d'acces securise aux
donnees (CASD). No observation can leave the enclave. Confidentiality restricts
the *data*, not the *code* : everything except the microdata is published here.

## What is available

**The full pipeline.** Cleaning, variable construction, and every specification,
in the order they run.

**A synthetic data generator.** It reproduces the structure of the source files
(the same variables, types, and plausible marginal distributions) with no real
observation. Clone the repository, run the pipeline on synthetic input, and the
whole chain executes. A referee can audit the logic without clearance.

**A metadata dictionary.** Every variable, its source file, and how it was built.

## What is not, and why

The microdata. Access runs through a CASD application.

## Why bother

Journals now require a data availability statement, and work on confidential
data usually answers with a paragraph of apology. A synthetic generator plus a
public pipeline is a better answer: it makes the claim checkable rather than
merely stated.
